mainEntity.name: My mother is diabetic. Can you handle special meals?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Before booking, we ask for a detailed medical form. We identify safe restaurants, avoid street sweets, and coordinate meal timing with insulin schedules. We're not nutritionists, but we're meticulous about dietary integrity.

mainEntity.name: Is travel insurance necessary for the Varanasi Gaya tour?

acceptedAnswer.text: Highly recommended, not mandatory. Most international health insurance covers India. If your parents don't have it, we can guide you to quick-purchase policies (often 3-5% of package cost). Cover medical evacuation and hospitalization.

mainEntity.name: Can my 82-year-old father with a walker participate in the pilgrimage?

acceptedAnswer.text: Absolutely. We'll arrange car access to temple entrances (where possible), accessible routes within temples, seating for darshan, extra assistance from our driver, and modified activities (skip stairs, reduce walking distances). The pilgrimage isn't diminished—it's adapted.

mainEntity.name: What if my parents want to extend the trip?

acceptedAnswer.text: Tell us. We can add days, adjust the pace, or shift focus. If they want to spend 3 days in Varanasi instead of 2, we reschedule. If they want to add Ayodhya or Mathura, we build it in. Flexibility is built into our model.

mainEntity.name: What if someone gets sick mid-trip?

acceptedAnswer.text: We have hospital partnerships in all three cities. We'll arrange doctor consultation (usually via WhatsApp video initially). If hospitalization is needed, we handle admissions, insurance coordination, and stay with your parents until discharge.

mainEntity.name: When is the best time to visit Varanasi, Gaya, and Prayagraj?

acceptedAnswer.text: October-February (winter) is ideal. Varanasi averages 20-25°C. March-May is hot (35-40°C). June-September is monsoon season. Winter is ideal for elderly pilgrims who tire easily in heat.

mainEntity.name: What is the ideal duration for Kashi Gaya Prayag tour?

acceptedAnswer.text: We recommend 4-5 days for a fatigue-free experience. While the circuit can be completed in 3 days, 4-5 days allows for proper rest periods critical for elderly travelers and deeper spiritual engagement at each site.

mainEntity.name: How much does the Varanasi Gaya Prayagraj tour package cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Our packages range from ₹32,000-55,000 per person depending on group size (2-6+ adults), hotel choice (3-star vs 4-star), and season (peak Oct-March vs off-season).

mainEntity.name: Do you arrange pind daan ceremony at Gaya?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, pind daan is the emotional centerpiece of Gaya pilgrimage. We connect you with certified priests at Vishnupad Temple, handle all logistics, and allocate 90 minutes minimum for this sacred ritual. We never rush ancestral rites.

mainEntity.name: Is the tour suitable for NRI families visiting from abroad?

acceptedAnswer.text: Absolutely. We specialize in NRI pilgrimage packages. We speak fluent English, offer WhatsApp video coordination across timezones, handle travel insurance assistance, and understand the unique challenges of returning to India after years abroad.

mainEntity.name: What hotels do you use for elderly pilgrims?

acceptedAnswer.text: We use personally vetted 3-4 star hotels with: elevated toilet seats, grab bars in bathrooms, non-slip floors, ground floor or elevator access, firm modern mattresses (critical for back pain), and 24-hour room service. Comfort isn't luxury for elderly—it's healthcare.

mainEntity.name: Can you arrange VIP darshan at Kashi Vishwanath Temple?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. We book early morning darshan slots (5:30-7 AM) when crowds are 90% lower, and leverage our local network for VIP entry lanes with valid documentation. We never force 2+ hour waits on elderly pilgrims.
